title: sync --to-store reported overwriting nothing and replacing the store in one breath, and its agreement verdict never examined an ADD
body:
**RE-PREMISED 2026-08-28 BY THE NODE WHOSE MEASUREMENT WITHDREW IT, on vc's GO, with lamplight-vc's agreement. THE ORIGINAL MECHANISM AND TITLE WERE WRONG. What is kept below is what survived, and what was struck is named so a reader can tell a withdrawal from an omission.**

## What was filed, and why it did not survive

The issue said `sync --to-store` compares the parsed model of both sides, so a lossy parser agrees with its own output and the repair never runs. **It said honestly that the mechanism was inferred rather than read.** It was read, and it is not that.

`facade.rs:2948 sync_overwrite` compares `store.load_canon()` against `ingest::read(&self.project)`, and **`ingest::read` walks `project.thread_json(&id)` -- `intent/.canon/st/ST####.json`. It never opens a markdown file.** Both sides are serde over JSON. There is no lossy parser on that path and no markdown on it either.

**Driven on a clean v3 fixture, both directions:**

- **Control -- the instrument fires.** Edit the `.canon` extract so it genuinely differs from the store: `warning: replacing the store from the extract OVERWRITES: ST0001: differs on disk`, then the write, and the store takes the new value. **The verb is not blind.**
- **The reported shape.** Plant an `intent/st/ST0001/acceptance.md` citing a path in flat disagreement with canon: `note: the store and the extract agree`. Correctly -- that file is not on the path.

**And the reporting estate settled it against its own filing.** lamplight-vc went past the discriminating read that was requested (it pointed at a path both accounts already agree is truncated, so it could not have separated them -- their catch) and established: `intent/st/ST0300/` does not exist; `.intentfiles` lists 16 WIP threads and ST0300 is not among them; the full citation is intact at `intent/st/COMPLETED/ST0300/acceptance.md:54`, a v2 status-bucket path canon has never seen. **So that `sync --to-store` compared the store against nothing and told the truth.** Their words: *they measured the verb, I measured a coincidence and named a cause for it.*

**The remedy the original proposed -- compare the raw stored text on both sides -- would have changed nothing**, because both sides are the same JSON. Building it would have left Lamplight's 74 rows exactly as broken with a green beside them.

## What survives, and it is FIXED at `557d220d`

Three strands, all measured on a clean v3 fixture, all true under either account of the Lamplight observation -- which is why this half was fixed while the rest went back.

1. **The verb printed both answers to the question it was asked.** `note: ... this restore overwrites nothing` immediately followed by `ok: store replaced from the extract, 1 thread(s)`. An operator checking whether a repair had run was told both, and **`replaced` is the one that reads as a result.** The result line now says `rewritten ... nothing the store already held was overwritten` when nothing was, and keeps `replaced` for when something was.

2. **The agreement verdict claimed more than it examined.** `sync_overwrite` walks the threads the STORE already holds and asks whether each still matches the extract. **A thread present in the extract and absent from the store is never reached -- it is an ADD -- so `the store and the extract agree` was false in exactly the case where the extract carries something new.** Driven: plant a `ST0002.json` the store has never seen, run the verb, and it prints agreement, reports `2 thread(s)`, and `st show ST0002` then answers from the store at rc=0. **The thread arrived under a message saying nothing would change.** Widening the check to DETECT the ADD is a change to a destructive verb's warning surface and was deliberately not done; the sentence now says what was examined and names the blind spot.

3. **The count was read as a claim about files.** lamplight-vc ran this on ST0300, saw `1 thread(s)`, and took it for the thread having been processed from its own directory -- a thread with no realised form at all. The count was true about the canon extract and false about everything the reader took it for. It now says `canon extract`.

**The regression test asserts the INVARIANT, not the wording:** if the run says it overwrote nothing, it must not also say the store was replaced. Its control is the other arm -- a genuine divergence must still produce the warning AND the word `replaced` -- without which the file is satisfied by a binary that stopped saying `replaced` at all, or by one whose `sync` stopped working.

## What is struck, and where it goes

**The mechanism, the title, and the proposed remedy are withdrawn.** The real blocker is the sentence the original wrote and walked past: **on a migrated estate there is no route from the authored v2 markdown into the store.** That is `0097`'s family, it is NEW WORK, and it is the actual gate on the Lamplight 74-row re-run -- **all ten damaged threads are Completed, so none is realised, so the intact markdown is unreachable by construction.**

## Sizing that route for hv's menu -- COSTED, NOT BUILT

**What already exists, which is more than the original assumed.** `Facade::ingest_from_md` calls `legacy::scan(project)` -- **the same migrator, carrying both citation fixes (`e935734d`, `eff618e8`).** The CLI arm prints the scan's residue and carried findings and then stops. **The reader is built and correct; the writer exists on the migration path; only the wiring and the semantics are missing.** `0097` is therefore not "an unbuilt parser" but "a built reader with no write".

**The hard part is not the wiring. It is what writing onto an ALREADY-migrated estate means.**

- **A -- `ingest --from-md` writes, whole estate. Size S.** Smallest wiring. **Wrong for this job**: it would overwrite every post-migration edit across the estate with v2 state. Cheap to build, destructive to use.
- **B -- scoped re-port by thread id. Size M.** Writes only named threads. Still whole-thread, so post-migration edits on those threads are lost. **Materially safer for THIS job than in general, because Lamplight's ten are all Completed** and unlikely to carry post-migration edits -- but that safety is a property of the corpus, not of the option.
- **C -- field-scoped repair. Size L.** Take only the AT citations from the v2 markdown for named threads and leave every other field alone. Safest, most work, and it needs a stated rule for a row present on one side and not the other.

**A PRECONDITION NONE OF THE THREE ESCAPES, AND IT IS UNVERIFIED:** the authored markdown for Lamplight's ten sits under `intent/st/COMPLETED/ST####/` -- a v2 STATUS BUCKET. `legacy::scan` presumably walks those, since that is how the original migration found them, **but that is an inference and not a measurement, and it decides whether any of the three works at all.** It is one drive on a fixture and it should happen before the menu is chosen, not after.

**Also unverified: whether the writer `migrate.rs` uses can be re-aimed at a subset**, which is what separates B and C from A.

## Not claimed

That the three strands fixed at `557d220d` were the whole of what an operator found confusing here. They are what reproduced.
